DashNovel User Guide

A writing app for authors who write every day. DashNovel turns your writing into a dashboard of honest numbers, and your manuscript never leaves your hands.

Getting Started

DashNovel runs on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. There is no account and no sign-in—open the app and start writing.

Your manuscripts are stored on your device. If you turn on iCloud sync, they are also stored in your own iCloud account and continue on your other devices. There is no developer server.

The screen

On iPhone, you move between four tabs at the bottom. Tap a tab, or swipe quickly sideways.

TabWhat it's for
DashboardSee how much you've written
LibraryCreate and organize projects, folders, and files
WritingWrite
SearchSearch across every project

On iPad and Mac, areas sit side by side: the Library on the left, the canvas where you write in the middle, and Search and the Dashboard on the right. Use the buttons in the top bar to show or hide each area. See On iPad and On Mac.

Your first project

In the Library, tap + to create a new project. A Writing folder and a first episode, "Episode 1," are created with it. You can also choose to add Characters, Objects, Timeline, and Blank Document folders.

Tips

The first time you visit a screen, it dims slightly and points to what to tap. Tap "OK" to close it. You can turn tips off or see them all again in Settings › Help.

Library

The Library organizes your writing into Project › Folder › File.

Creating

Tap + and choose one of three:

CreateWhat it is
New WritingA manuscript file. One file per episode
New FileA file that isn't manuscript—choose Characters, Objects, Timeline, or Blank Document
New FolderGroups files, like Volume 1 and Volume 2. Up to five levels deep

If you select a folder in the list first, the new item goes inside it.

File types

TypeWhat you writeStatistics
WritingThe actual manuscriptCounted
CharactersCharacter cards—photo, name, subtitle, attributes, notesNot counted
ObjectsCards for items, places, and lore—same layout as CharactersNot counted
TimelineA chronology built from blocksNot counted
Blank DocumentResearch and idea notes. Same editor as WritingNot counted

Written, Typed, and Writing time are counted only in Writing files. However much research you write, your manuscript record doesn't move.

Select, open, and move

  • Tap once to select, and tap again to open. Tap the gear in a selected row to change its name, icon, tags, or whether it's excluded from statistics.
  • Touch and hold, then drag, to move. Drag up or down to change the order, sideways to change the folder level. Pause over a collapsed folder to expand it.
  • Add tags to filter by them in Search. Manage tags in Settings › Tags.

Trash

Deleted folders and files stay in the Trash for 30 days. Restore them from Settings › Trash and they return to where they were. While a file is in the Trash, its words leave your statistics; restoring it brings them back.

Archive

Move projects you aren't working on out of the project list with Project Settings › Move to Archive. The manuscript, lock, and statistics stay the same, and you can bring a project back from Archive at the bottom of the project list. In the Archive, you can also choose per project whether it counts toward your statistics.

Writing

Open a Writing file from the Library to open the editor. When you reopen the app, the Writing file you last worked on is already open.

Saving

DashNovel saves automatically when you pause typing, and also when you switch tabs or leave the app. Tap the save button in the menu bar to keep that moment as a manual backup (the latest 10 per file).

Formatting

Use bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and left, center, right, or justified alignment. Change them from the formatting group in the menu bar or from the menu that appears when you select text. With a hardware keyboard, ⌘B, ⌘I, and ⌘U also work.

  • Text color and highlight: pick a color from the two buttons in the menu bar. Highlights are applied to selected text.
  • Divider: insert a short line, three dots, or a wave where a scene changes. Press Delete at the start of the line right below a divider to remove just the divider.

Inside DashNovel (copy and paste, backups, sync), formatting comes along. When you paste into another app, only meaningful formatting like bold and italic goes with it. Turn off Copy with Formatting in Settings › Writing to copy plain text.

Automatic replacements

  • Type three periods to get a single ellipsis (…). Undo right away to get the three periods back.
  • Smart quotes: typing an opening quote adds the closing quote with the cursor in between. When you finish a line of dialogue and press Return, you skip past the closing quote to the next line.
  • Smart brackets: ( { [ < close the same way.

Turn each off in Settings › Writing. Characters closed automatically count toward Typed just as if you'd typed them.

Find and replace

Open it with the magnifying glass in the menu bar. Matches are highlighted, and the up and down arrows move between them. Replace one at a time or all at once—a single undo reverts Replace All. It works the same in Characters, Timeline, and Blank Documents.

Undo

Text you type continuously is undone in chunks that break at the end of a sentence, a new line, or a short pause (Mac and iPad with a hardware keyboard). Undo and redo don't count toward Typed.

The count line

Tap the character count above the editor to change the basis (with spaces, without spaces, manuscript pages, words, and more). When text is selected, it shows "selected / total."

Text appearance

Use Aa in the menu bar to change the font, size, line spacing, paragraph spacing, indent, and text scale. This only changes how text looks on screen—your saved text and exported files aren't affected. You can change the same things in Settings › Writing.

Jump to the top or bottom

Swipe hard through a long manuscript and buttons to jump to the top or bottom briefly appear at the edge of the screen.

Copy all text

Tap the copy button in the menu bar to copy the whole file. Use it when you paste into a publishing platform.

Writing status and Final lock

Every Writing file has a status.

StatusWhen it changes
PendingRight after the file is created
DraftingAutomatically, once text comes in
Revising · EditingYou change it
FinalYou change it—the text is locked

Setting a file to Final locks the text so you can't change a finished manuscript by accident. Find, copy, and export still work. To edit again, change the status back to something other than Final.

Memos

Memos are small notes pinned beside your manuscript. Each episode has its own, and they aren't counted in statistics.

  • Create: tap the round memo button in the editor, or "Add Memo" in the menu bar.
  • Pin to text: select text and add a memo from the menu. The text gets a highlight and the memo is attached to it. A small note mark appears at the end of the pinned text; tap the highlight to open the memo.
  • View: tap the round memo button to list that episode's memos, and choose one to open its card at the top of the screen.
  • In the Library, tap the memo badge beside an episode to show its memos. You can drag a memo to another episode.
  • Deleted memos go to Settings › Trash.

Characters, Objects, and Timeline

Characters and Objects are card lists. Tap a card to expand it, and add a name, subtitle, notes, and a photo.

  • Attributes: add fields like age, height, or job to each card. Tap the gear on a card to add, remove, and reorder attributes. Save sets you use often in Settings › Attributes and add them all at once.
  • Touch and hold a card, then drag, to reorder. You can tag cards too.

Timeline is a chronology of event blocks. Each block has a title and body, and you drag to reorder. Find searches every block, even collapsed ones.

Blank Documents hold research and ideas. The editor is the same as Writing, but there are no statistics, writing status, or timer.

Reading Your Statistics

Know what these four numbers mean and the rest is easy.

NameMeaning
TypedCharacters you actually typed—including ones you later deleted. Once counted, it never goes down. Undo and redo are left out
WrittenThe text that remains now, counted on the day each character was written
EfficiencyWritten ÷ Typed. Shows how much you rewrote
Writing timeTime you actually spent editing. It stops after five minutes without input

Written can go down. If you delete today a paragraph you wrote yesterday, yesterday's Written goes down—not today's. It measures "what you wrote that day that still survives."

  • Pasted text counts as written at the moment you paste it.
  • Files in the Trash are left out and come back when restored.
  • The numbers are the same on every device.

Counting basis

Choose with spaces, without spaces, all characters, manuscript pages, or words in Settings › Statistics & Goals. For manuscript pages, choose 200 or 400 characters per page. Goals are shown in the unit of the basis you choose.

Leaving imported writing out of your statistics

If you paste an old manuscript in all at once, it counts as written today. Pick the option that fits.

OptionWhereWhen
Reset StatisticsSettings › Statistics & GoalsRight after bringing in old manuscripts when you start out. Records before that moment are left out (can't be undone)
Excluded daysSettings › Statistics & GoalsA single day that spiked. Leaves out that day's records
Exclude from statsFile settings · Project settingsLeaves out one file or project, past records included

When your day starts

Change "Day starts at" in Settings › Statistics & Goals to something like 4:00, and writing at 3 a.m. counts toward the previous day.

Dashboard

Build your dashboard from the blocks you want.

BlockWhat it shows
Goal ProgressHow much of today's, this week's, and this month's goal you've met
Written per HourCharacters kept per hour of writing
RecordsEverything you've written, best records, and character count
Written TrendWritten and goals by day, week, or month
Writing Time StatsWriting time and your golden hours
EfficiencyHow much of what you typed you kept
Goal CalendarWhether you met your daily goal each day
AchievementsStreak tiers and trophies
Manuscript ProgressEpisodes per writing status, and Finals this week
CalendarEvents, D-days, and daily goals
To DoA to-do list and its progress
TimerWriting timer (iPad and Mac)
  • Edit: touch and hold a block, or tap the edit button in the top strip, to open Edit Dashboard. Remove and drag to reorder in the top list; tap in the lower list to add. A dot on the edit button means new blocks are available.
  • Details: tap a chart, ring, or achievement to open a detailed table by day or by file. Pinch a chart to show a longer or shorter period.

Share Card

Use the share button at the left of the top strip to turn your record into a manuscript-paper card and share it. Choose the period (today, this week, this month, and more) and which numbers to show. Project and file names are never included.

Goals and Achievements

Set daily, weekly, and monthly goals in Settings › Statistics & Goals. The defaults are 5,000 / 30,000 / 120,000 characters. You can also change them right away with the gear on the Goal Progress block. A new goal applies from the current period; results for past periods stay as they were.

Achievements are tiers and trophies earned by meeting your goal in a row. To count, the goal for that period must be at least 3,000 characters a day (700 words a day if you count words), with at least an hour of writing time a day. Weekly is five times that, monthly twenty.

Writing Timer

On iPhone, set it with the alarm clock in the editor's menu bar; on iPad and Mac, use the Timer block on the dashboard. You can set anything from 1 minute to 8 hours 59 minutes.

  • The timer applies to the whole app and keeps running when you open another file.
  • When it ends, a sound plays and the screen briefly flashes. Choose the sound and flash under "When It Ends" in the timer.
  • On iPhone and iPad, it pauses when you leave the app and resumes when you return—so it doesn't run while you aren't writing.
  • The timer has nothing to do with Writing time, which only builds up when you actually type.

Search

Search finds things across every project at once: file and folder names and text, Characters and Objects (name, subtitle, notes, attributes), Timeline blocks, and memos. Narrow to one project, or choose tags to keep only items that have all of them.

Tap a result to open the file with the matches highlighted.

Export

Select a folder or Writing file in the Library and tap Export in its settings. You can also open it from Settings › Export.

FormatUse it for
.txtPasting into a publishing platform. The safest
.docxWord, Pages, contest submissions
.hwpxHancom Hangul (2014 or later)
.pdfFixed layout for reading and review
.epubE-book apps
.mdNote apps that use Markdown
  • Single file combines every episode; One file per episode creates several files. When splitting, you can bundle them into one ZIP.
  • Formatting (bold, italic, and so on) and text color are included as far as the format supports. Highlights are working marks and are left out.
  • Only Writing files are exported. Characters, Timeline, and Blank Documents aren't manuscript and are left out.

Sync and Backups

iCloud sync

Turn iCloud Sync on or off in Settings › General, separately on each device. When it's on, your manuscripts, statistics, and some settings are stored in your own iCloud account, and iPhone, iPad, and Mac on the same account show the same manuscripts.

  • The status line in Settings shows uploading, downloading, or up to date.
  • If DashNovel notices the account changed or your iCloud data was deleted, it stops and asks what to do. It never deletes the manuscripts on your device.
  • A device with sync turned off stores only on that device. Deleting the app there deletes its manuscripts too—keep sync on, or export important manuscripts.

Auto Backup

While you write, DashNovel backs up changed files every hour. Backups stay on that device and aren't synced.

  • If the same text is edited on two devices at once and one version loses, the lost version is kept as a backup and you're told.
  • See backups in Settings › General › Auto Backup, or with the backup button in the editor. Restore a backup, extract it as a new file, or copy all of its text.
  • Before restoring, the current text is backed up first.

Lock

  • App Lock: turn it on in Settings › General › Lock. The app asks for Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode when it opens. You can also choose when it locks again (immediately, after 1 minute, after 5 minutes, and more).
  • Project Lock: turn it on in Project settings. You confirm each time you enter that project, and apart from its name, a locked project stays hidden in Search, detailed statistics, and the Trash.

Themes, Fonts, and Language

  • Theme: choose from 17 in Settings › Theme. Each has a light and dark version, and Dark mode there lets you choose Off, On, or Use OS Setting.
  • Fonts: choose from RIDIBatang (default), Pretendard, MaruBuri, Iropke Batang, or the system font. On iPhone and iPad you can import font files from the Files app; on Mac, you can choose any font installed on that Mac.
  • Language: change it in Settings › General › Language. DashNovel is available in English, Korean, Japanese, Chinese (Traditional and Simplified), Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Italian, Indonesian, and Vietnamese.

On iPad

iPad shows the Library, canvas, Search, and Dashboard side by side.

  • Top bar: the buttons on the left show or hide the Library and the two-pane canvas; the buttons on the right show or hide Search and the Dashboard. An area that's showing has an underline. If there isn't room, the area on the other side closes.
  • Two-finger swipe: swipe sideways with two fingers over the canvas or Library to slide areas in and out.
  • Two-pane canvas: when the screen is wide enough, open two files side by side. Touch and hold a pane's header bar, then drag, to swap sides; drag the divider to change widths.
  • Paper view: turn on paper from the view menu in a pane's header bar, and the text width stops at a page width even in a very wide pane, so it's easier to read.
  • Keyboard and pointer: with a hardware keyboard, use the menu bar at the top of the screen and the same shortcuts as on Mac. With a trackpad or mouse, use right-click menus.
  • The timer lives in the Timer block on the dashboard.

On Mac

On Mac, one window holds the Library and Info, the canvas, and Search and the Dashboard side by side. Show or hide areas with the buttons in the top bar or the View menu, and drag the dividers to change widths.

  • Two-pane canvas: split into two panes with ⌘\. Drag a file from the Library onto a pane to open it, and double-click a pane's header bar to enlarge that pane.
  • Page View: see your text laid out on paper with ⌥⌘P in the View menu. Choose a paper size (A4, B5, and more), Spread Pages, and page numbers.
  • Find window: open the floating find window with ⌘F. It can search both panes at once.
  • Right-click: use menus for renaming, formatting, text color, highlights, adding memos, and more in the Library, canvas, and cards.
  • Opening from the Library: choose Double-click or Single-click in Settings › General › Library.

Subscription

  • Free: edit one project up to 10,000 characters (with spaces). No features are locked—sync, themes, lock, export, and the dashboard are free too.
  • With several projects, only the one you wrote in most recently can be edited; the rest are read-only. Past 10,000 characters, that project becomes read-only too.
  • Subscribe to edit with no limit on projects or length. The first month is a free trial.
  • When a subscription ends, your manuscripts are never deleted. Reading, search, copy, export, and sync keep working.
  • Use Settings › Subscription to manage your subscription, redeem a code, or restore purchases. On another device or after reinstalling, your subscription usually comes back on its own; tap Restore Purchases if it doesn't.

FAQ

How do I know my writing was saved?
DashNovel saves automatically when you pause. Tap the save button in the menu bar to also keep that moment as a manual backup.

I wrote long character notes, but Written didn't go up.
That's expected. Statistics only count Writing files.

I deleted text I wrote yesterday, and yesterday's Written went down.
That's by design. Written counts "what you wrote that day that still remains."

I brought in an old manuscript and today's Written jumped.
Right after bringing it in, tap Reset Statistics in Settings › Statistics & Goals. See "Leaving imported writing out of your statistics" above.

If I paste back a manuscript fixed by a spell checker, does Typed go up by the whole manuscript?
No. If you select the original text and paste over it, or paste right where you just deleted it, only the characters that actually changed are counted as new. Deleted text is remembered only while the app stays open.

Why can't I see Apple's Writing Tools in Writing files?
Writing Tools rewrites whole paragraphs as if newly typed, which would erase when you originally wrote them—so they're off in Writing files. You can use them in Blank Documents.

What happens to my writing if I delete the app?
The writing on that device is deleted with it. If iCloud sync was on, it stays in your iCloud account and comes back when you reinstall and turn sync on. Also export important manuscripts and keep them separately.
